data.narrative:
Path Robotics, a Series D robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $271M to date, is evaluated against a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable in the robotics sector. The peer set includes same-stage and adjacent-stage companies: Exotec ($2.0B Series D), Hadrian ($1.6B Series D), Divergent ($2.3B Series E), Agile Robots ($1.0B Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B Series C).

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach, using total capital raised as a baseline proxy, applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement, yielding $406M. The peer-median method triangulates off five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, establishing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.3B.

Synthesizing these two methods produces a triangulated range of $346M (low) to $1.8B (high), with a median point of $1.0B. The low-end reflects stage-progression methodology alone; the high-end anchors to peer maximum valuations. Key uncertainties include Path Robotics' revenue scale and unit economics relative to peers, stage-specific valuation step-up precedent within the manufacturing robotics subsector, and whether peer multiples reflect sustainable market positioning or capital-driven appreciation.
